flashcard_questions.q: Which 1911 Act covered only working men, not their families?
Which wartime service, set up in 1939, proved a state-run health system could work?
Who wrote the 1942 report that proposed a welfare state from the cradle to the grave?
Which of Beveridge's five giants meant poor housing?
Which of Beveridge's five giants meant unemployment?
Which party won the 1945 general election in a landslide?
Who was appointed Minister for Health and given the task of building the NHS?
On what date did the NHS officially begin?
Which NHS principle means treatment is paid for through taxation, never billed to patients?
flashcard_questions.a: Free at the point of delivery.

flashcard_questions.q: Which NHS principle means the service is open to everyone regardless of wealth?
In January 1948, ____% of BMA members said they would refuse to join the new service.
What did Bevan say he had done to win the doctors over?
flashcard_questions.a: He had 'stuffed their mouths with gold'.

flashcard_questions.q: What key concession did Bevan give hospital consultants?
flashcard_questions.a: They could keep private practice alongside their NHS work.

flashcard_questions.q: How many pairs of spectacles were issued in the NHS's first year?

flashcard_questions.a: Charges were introduced for dental treatment and spectacles.

notes: 15 cards: 5 event/law, 4 principle or term, 3 person, 2 figure (one cloze), 1 quotation. Kept only two of Beveridge's five giants so the fronts stay uniquely identifying.
